steps.text: Combine evaporated milk, brown sugar, butter, egg yolks, and vanilla in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring constantly, at a low boil until mixture turns a light caramel color and thickens, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in coconut and pecans. Let cool to room temperature before spreading on cake.
Use to frost a German chocolate cake. Serve and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: German Chocolate Cake Frosting
raw_recipe.description: This German chocolate cake frosting is made from scratch with coconut and pecans for a thick and creamy topping perfect on German chocolate cake.

video.description: Ever wondered what goes into that decadent German chocolate cake frosting? In this video, we'll show you how to make that frosting to perfection. A mixture of evaporated milk, brown sugar, egg yolks, butter, and vanilla are cooked up until nice and thick. Then just add chopped pecans and flaked coconut and let the frosting cool to room temperature. Spread on chocolate cake and you're dessert is set!

review.reviewBody:
This frosting recipe was easy and turned out fabulous. Make sure you cook over medium to medium heat while stirring constantly to obtain a thick consistancy. I'm a grandma and the smell of the brown sugar, milk, eggs and butter cooking reminded me of my first job in the summer of 1963 where I made carmel corn from scratch each day.
This recipe is well worth the little extra effort.

I'm so glad I made this recipe and not one of the others that were on this site. This one looked a lot easier but didn't have as many ratings. I decided to give this one a try and it was wonderful! My husband loves German Chocolate cake and so I made it for his birthday. I decided to go for a home made frosting instead of out of the can, and I'm glad I did. This is easy to make. I boiled it for about 20 minutes on medium, added the nuts and coconut and let cool. I didn't have to add anything to get it to be thick enough, like I read about in other reviews of other recipes. This one turned out great and my husband loved it!
Wonderful frosting! The key to this thickening up is to stir and cook over medium heat for about 12 minutes.

Perfect 1st time. Used 12 oz evaporated milk, 3/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup white granulated sugar, 4 egg yolks, and 2 teaspoons vanilla. This is like making custard to keep the eggs from "scrambling" during cooking. I used a 6 quart Dutch oven over low heat and constantly stirred for about 10 minutes. I can see where using a smaller sauce pan can take much longer. 

Toasted coconut flakes and chopped pecans together in baking pan for 15 minutes at 325 deg. until golden brown prior to mixing in. OMG, we were eating warm frosting out of the Dutch oven.

Wow, this was absolutely fantastic! I made it for German Chocolate Cupcakes for my mom's birthday. My only suggestion is to wait until you pull it off the stove to add the vanilla. Otherwise, it is perfect as is. I did follow other reviewers suggestions to cook over Low for 10-12 minutes. Then it thickens as it cools. We have some non-coconutters in the fam so I left out the coconut. I toasted the pecans, too. Thank you for a wonderful recipe!

I substituted the coconut and just used 2 cups chopped pecans since we do not care for dried coconut. Came out great. Also I made muffins because it is easier to share them than it is a slice of cake. LCP

I tweaked the recipe just a bit. Like some others mentioned I toasted the coconut and the nuts ( didn’t have enough pecans so I supplemented with almonds). I also added 1/2 tsp of salt and 1/2 tsp butter flavoring.

Thanks so much for this recipe. It turned out great for us! My husband says he will now request this frosting for when we bake chocolate cakes. Notes for me: 1- a can of 354 ml evaporated milk is about 1.5 Cups, so to use the whole can, make sure to increase all other ingredients by a factor of 1.5 (could be why some result in runny consistency). 2-Our store only sells 200g sweetened shredded coconut, so I reduced sugar by half and used the whole package as husband doesn't like pecans (weird! who doesn't love pecans?)

Loved it! I usually don't eat german chocolate cake, but I love this. I adjusted the recipe for 16 servings and it was perfect. Instead of heating all the ingredients together, I melted the butter and then added the remaining wet ingredients. I also used rum instead of vanilla. Like some of the other readers I decided to lightly toast the coconut and pecans. My family loved it.
I have only made double the amount and it takes significantly longer to thicken up, atleast 20-30 minutes.
This recipe was easy & delicious. I put on cake & then under the broiler for a minute or two to toast the coconut like my grandma use to do.

This is the best German chocolate cake frosting I’ve ever made. For a layer cake I might add a few more tablespoons of evaporated milk the next time I make it the frosting would drip over the edge a little better
Outstanding
I added the vanilla after I removed it from the great and let it cool a bit!!ot makes a lot but it’s not wasted!!
I will make it again.
Super yummy and easy to follow recipe! My husband LOVES German chocolate cake but can't have nuts so I omitted the pecans and added extra coconut. He enjoyed his birthday cake very much!

Vanilla shouldn't be boiled. That should be added after you boil it. I tried the way the recipe was written and ended up adding another 1/2 tsp of vanilla after I added the coconut because it didn't taste right. The extra vanilla helped some. I also added a could dashes of salt because I didn't add nuts. (treenut allergy in my house). Maybe not using the nuts changed the flavor more than I anticipated, but the flavor wasn't one I will crave.

I do homemade scratch cakes/ donuts for the flea market as a side hustle and people special order from so lady wanted a German chocolate cake for mother's birthday, o never made one before so I tackled and your frosting Recipe was a hit with i did a 2 layer 9 inch cake and doubled the frosting the lady was in awe over it,thank you for the easy recipe, I followed it and ir was beautiful and excellent taste, this is my go to frosting, again thank you,I wanted to share the pic but couldn't find to upload Donna Hinson Heavenly Delight Cakes
Made it exactly as listed. Including being for 10 minutes. Perfect. More than enough frosting for 9×13 so assume it would easily cover 2 layers. Packed the brown sugar.
I made this recipe just as written--no changes! It is just delicious! It was easy to mix up and cook. Tastes like my Grandmother's recipe! Will make this often.
